title: 8 · Flash thickness: fill against load
level: Advanced · 3D · built-in die set · thin-flash refinement · ~7 min per run
summary: The 1"-8 hex bolt head of demo 4, forged with three flash-land thicknesses: the classic closed-die trade-off between die fill and press load.
instructions: 1. The die set is the hex bolt head (full model, flat and cylindrical die faces). The flash land is 3/16" wide; its thickness is the input 'Flash land thickness' under Geometry.

2. Run its multi-run: the flash thickness is swept from 1/32" to 1/8" with the same billet, material and press, so only the flash changes. Thin-flash refinement (Advanced) is on so the solver resolves the flash.
3. Compare peak load and final fill in RUNS, or Export ▸ Comparison report for the table and a peak-load / fill chart against flash thickness.
4. A thin flash chokes the outflow: the pressure in the cavity rises, the hex corners fill, and the load climbs steeply in the last millimetres.
5. A thick flash lets metal escape: lower load, but the corners may not fill. Die designers pick the thinnest flash the press can push.

6. Read the Volume change column too: the thinnest flash is only a few elements thick, so some volume is lost and the load difference is understated. A finer element size h sharpens the trend at the cost of run time.
